title: 1 John Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 John chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 John Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 John Chapter 4.

questions.question: In 1 John 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Ye are of God, little children
questions.correctAnswer: Beloved, believe not every spirit
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in the chapter, found in 1 John 4:1.

questions.question: What should we try according to 1 John 4?
questions.correctAnswer: The spirits
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:1 instructs us to try the spirits whether they are of God.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4, what signifies a spirit of God?
options: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh
Every spirit that speaks of the world
questions.correctAnswer: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:2 states that this confession indicates a spirit of God.

questions.question: What spirit is associated with those who confess not that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh?
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of antichrist
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:3 identifies this as the spirit of antichrist.

questions.question: Who does John say has overcome them?
questions.correctAnswer: The children of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:4 refers to 'little children' as those who have overcome.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4, who hears those who are of God?
questions.correctAnswer: He that knoweth God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:6 states that he who knows God hears us.

questions.question: What does love signify according to 1 John 4?
questions.correctAnswer: It is of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7 explains that love is of God.

questions.question: What are the false prophets described as in 1 John 4?
questions.correctAnswer: Of the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:5 states that they are of the world.

questions.question: What should we do according to 1 John 4:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Let us love one another
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7 directly instructs us to love one another.

questions.question: What is greater according to 1 John 4:4?
options: He that is in the world
Greater is he that is in you
questions.correctAnswer: Greater is he that is in you
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:4 states that greater is he that is in you than he that is in the world.

questions.question: What do those who are of the world do according to 1 John 4:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Speak of the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:5 tells us that those who are of the world speak of the world.

questions.question: True or False: Every spirit that confesseth Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: This statement is directly supported by 1 John 4:2.

questions.question: True or False: Those who know God hear us, according to 1 John 4.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:6 confirms that those who know God hear us.

questions.question: True or False: The spirit of God speaks only to the world.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not state that the spirit of God speaks only to the world; rather, it speaks to those who know God.

questions.question: True or False: Love is of the world according to 1 John 4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7 clearly states that love is of God, not of the world.

medium.title: 1 John Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 John Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:8, what is the fundamental nature of God?
questions.correctAnswer: God is love
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:8 states 'God is love,' which defines the fundamental nature of God.

questions.question: What does 1 John 4:12 promise will happen if someone loves one another, as commanded in 1 John 4:11?
options: God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
questions.correctAnswer: God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:12 promises that if we love one another (1 John 4:11), God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

questions.question: What was the purpose of God sending His only begotten Son into the world, according to 1 John 4:9?
options: That we might live through him
That we might judge the world
That we might conquer sin by our own strength
That we might receive earthly riches
questions.correctAnswer: That we might live through him
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:9 explains that God sent His Son so that we might live through Him.

questions.question: How does 1 John 4:10 explain the nature of love compared to 1 John 4:9?
options: Love is shown not by our love for God but by His love for us sending His Son
Love is earned by our good deeds
Love is only for those who believe perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Love is shown not by our love for God but by His love for us sending His Son
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:10 clarifies that love is not that we loved God, but that He loved us and sent His Son as propitiation, building on 1 John 4:9.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:13, what is the evidence that we dwell in God and He in us?
options: He hath given us of his Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: He hath given us of his Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:13 says we know we dwell in God because He has given us His Spirit.

questions.question: What practical command follows from God's love for us in 1 John 4:11?
options: We ought also to love one another
questions.correctAnswer: We ought also to love one another
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:11 commands that because God loved us, we also ought to love one another.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:14, what do believers testify about the Father and the Son?
options: The Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
The Son was sent to condemn the world
The Father sent the Son to bring riches
The Son came to bring political power
questions.correctAnswer: The Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:14 states believers testify that the Father sent the Son to save the world.

questions.question: Why does 1 John 4:8 say someone who does not love does not know God?
options: Because love is a feeling only
questions.correctAnswer: Because God is love
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:8 teaches that not loving means not knowing God, because God is love.

questions.question: How does 1 John 4:7 link love and knowledge of God?
options: Every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God
Love is unrelated to knowing God
Love is a test for prophets only
questions.correctAnswer: Every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7 states that love originates from God and those who love are born of God and know Him.

questions.question: What does 1 John 4:1 instruct believers to do regarding spirits?
options: Try the spirits whether they are of God
questions.correctAnswer: Try the spirits whether they are of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:1 commands believers to test spirits to discern if they are from God.

questions.question: What is the key test of the Spirit of God according to 1 John 4:2?
options: Confessing that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Confessing that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:2 explains that the Spirit of God is recognized by confessing Jesus Christ came in the flesh.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:4, why have believers overcome the spirits of the world?
options: Because greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world
Because believers are stronger than others
questions.correctAnswer: Because greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:4 states believers overcome because God within is greater than the spirit in the world.

questions.question: Why does 1 John 4:6 say some do not hear the message of God?
options: Because they are not of God
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are not of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:6 says those not of God do not hear the message of God.

questions.question: True or False: 1 John 4:14 indicates that the believers have seen and testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:14 confirms believers have seen and testify to the Father's sending of the Son as Saviour.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 John 4:3, every spirit that acknowledges Jesus Christ coming in the flesh is not of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:3 states that spirits denying Jesus Christ's coming in the flesh are not of God, so the statement is false.

hard.title: 1 John Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 John Chapter 4.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:15, what is the result when someone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God?
options: God dwelleth in him, and he in God
He shall be saved from judgment
He shall receive the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: God dwelleth in him, and he in God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:15 states, 'Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God.' This directly links confession with mutual indwelling.

questions.question: In 1 John 4:16, how is 'God' described in relation to love?
options: God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him
God is just; and he that obeys is loved by Him
God is merciful; and He shows mercy to the humble
God is holy; and He hates sin
questions.correctAnswer: God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:16 explicitly says, 'God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him,' emphasizing the identity of God with love.

questions.question: What is the significance of love being 'made perfect' according to 1 John 4:17?
options: It gives us boldness in the day of judgment
It guarantees no suffering in this life
questions.correctAnswer: It gives us boldness in the day of judgment
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:17 says, 'Herein is our love made perfect, that we may have boldness in the day of judgment,' showing the perfected love empowers confidence before God.

questions.question: In 1 John 4:18, what effect does 'perfect love' have on fear?
questions.correctAnswer: Perfect love casteth out fear
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:18 states, 'There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear,' indicating that mature love eliminates fear.

questions.question: According to 1 John 4:19, why do we love God?
options: Because we are afraid of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Because he first loved us
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:19 clearly says, 'We love him, because he first loved us,' establishing God's initiative in love.

questions.question: What does 1 John 4:20 say about a person who claims to love God but hates his brother?
questions.correctAnswer: He is a liar
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:20 states, 'If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar,' which condemns the inconsistency of such a claim.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'dwelleth' (μένει) in 1 John 4:16 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: To remain or abide continuously
questions.explanation: 'Dwelleth' (μένει) in 1 John 4:16 means 'to remain or abide continuously,' indicating a permanent, ongoing presence as used in the verse.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in 1 John 4:16: 'God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him'?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:16 employs chiasmus by mirroring the structure 'God is love' and 'dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him,' creating a symmetrical pattern.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of 'God is love' found in 1 John 4:8?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 6:5
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 6:5 commands to 'love the LORD your God,' which undergirds the New Testament theme in 1 John 4:8 that 'God is love,' reflecting covenant love.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the concept of love as sacrifice found in 1 John 4:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 5:8
questions.explanation: Romans 5:8 states, 'God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us,' fulfilling the sacrificial love theme of 1 John 4:10.

questions.question: What immediately precedes 1 John 4:15, which speaks of confessing Jesus as the Son of God?
options: Testimony that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
A command to love one another
An exhortation to try the spirits
questions.correctAnswer: Testimony that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:14 immediately precedes verse 15 and says, 'And we have seen and do testify that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world,' setting the foundation for confession in verse 15.

questions.question: How does 1 John 4:12 use typology to explain God's presence in believers?
options: No man hath seen God at any time; if we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
God appeared to Moses in the burning bush
Jesus is the image of the invisible God
The temple is a shadow of heavenly things
questions.correctAnswer: No man hath seen God at any time; if we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:12 uses the typology of unseen God being made manifest through love among believers, indicating God’s presence is perfected by mutual love.

questions.question: What does 1 John 4:4 mean by 'greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world'?
options: The Spirit of God within believers is greater than worldly spirits
Believers are more powerful than kings
The angels are mightier than demons
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of God within believers is greater than worldly spirits
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:4 emphasizes that the Spirit of God dwelling in believers is stronger than any spirit in the world, indicating spiritual victory.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'fear' in 1 John 4:18 differ from the Hebrew word 'yirah' often translated as fear in the Old Testament?
options: 1 John 4:18 refers to fear as torment and separation, while 'yirah' often denotes reverential awe
Both mean fear of physical harm
1 John 4:18 uses fear to mean respect, 'yirah' means dread
questions.correctAnswer: 1 John 4:18 refers to fear as torment and separation, while 'yirah' often denotes reverential awe
questions.explanation: In 1 John 4:18, fear is described negatively as torment, contrasting the Hebrew 'yirah,' which frequently connotes reverent awe of God.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 John 4:21, the commandment from God is that he who loves God must also love his brother.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:21 explicitly states, 'And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also,' confirming this commandment is from God.

theological.title: 1 John Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 John Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 4:2 teach about the incarnation of Christ?
options: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God
Jesus Christ is a spirit and not truly flesh
The flesh is a hindrance to salvation
Jesus Christ only appeared to come in the flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:2 clearly teaches that a true confession of Jesus Christ includes acknowledging that He has come in the flesh, affirming the doctrine of the incarnation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 4:10 teach about the nature of God's love and atonement?
options: Love is primarily demonstrated by God sending His Son as propitiation for our sins
Humans must first love God before He loves them
God’s love depends on human obedience
Jesus’ sacrifice was a mere example, not atonement
questions.correctAnswer: Love is primarily demonstrated by God sending His Son as propitiation for our sins
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:10 teaches that God's love is shown not because we loved Him first, but because He sent His Son as propitiation, emphasizing substitutionary atonement as the ground of divine love.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christian assurance and union with God is taught in 1 John 4:13?
options: We know we dwell in Him and He in us because He has given us His Spirit
Assurance comes only through works and obedience
God’s presence is only experienced after death
The Spirit is a metaphor, not a real gift
questions.correctAnswer: We know we dwell in Him and He in us because He has given us His Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:13 explains that the indwelling of God and the believer’s assurance of this union comes through the gift of the Spirit, a foundational truth for Christian assurance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 4:8 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Love
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:8 states 'God is love,' directly attributing the divine attribute of love to God.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 4:14 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty in sending the Son to save the world
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty in sending the Son to save the world
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:14 emphasizes that the Father sent the Son as Savior of the world, highlighting God's sovereign initiative in salvation.

questions.question: How does 1 John 4:1–3 connect to the broader biblical theme of discerning true and false teachers?
options: It teaches the necessity of testing spirits to avoid antichrist deception, preparing believers for ongoing spiritual vigilance
It encourages blind faith without questioning
It rejects the incarnation as a test of truth
It limits spiritual discernment only to apostles
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches the necessity of testing spirits to avoid antichrist deception, preparing believers for ongoing spiritual vigilance
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:1–3 instructs believers to test spirits because many false prophets have gone out, connecting to the biblical call for discernment (cf. Matthew 7:15).

questions.question: In what way does 1 John 4:7–8 prepare for the New Testament teaching on love as the fruit of the Spirit?
options: It identifies love as originating from God and as evidence of knowing God, aligning with Galatians 5's fruit of the Spirit
It teaches love is optional for believers
It denies God’s involvement in love
It separates love from knowledge of God
questions.correctAnswer: It identifies love as originating from God and as evidence of knowing God, aligning with Galatians 5's fruit of the Spirit
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7–8 connects love to being born of God and knowing God, which corresponds with the Spirit-produced fruit of love found in Galatians 5.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 4:4 and 1 John 4:18 teach about love and spiritual victory?
options: Greater is He in us than in the world, and perfect love casts out fear which leads to victory over spiritual opposition
Fear is necessary for love to function
The world’s spirit is stronger than the Spirit in believers
questions.correctAnswer: Greater is He in us than in the world, and perfect love casts out fear which leads to victory over spiritual opposition
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:4 states that greater is He who is in believers than in the world, and 4:18 explains perfect love casts out fear, together teaching that love empowered by God enables spiritual victory.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 4:12 and 1 John 4:16 teach about God's indwelling and the believer's experience of love?
options: If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and God is love; thus, dwelling in love means dwelling in God
God can be seen physically if we love one another
Love is unrelated to God's presence
God dwells only in perfect believers without love
questions.correctAnswer: If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and God is love; thus, dwelling in love means dwelling in God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:12 teaches that loving one another is evidence of God's indwelling, while 4:16 states God is love and those who dwell in love dwell in God, linking love and divine presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 John 4:19 and 1 John 4:21 teach about the motivation and command of Christian love?
options: We love because God first loved us, and the commandment is to love both God and brother
We must love ourselves before God
Hating a brother is acceptable if we love God
questions.correctAnswer: We love because God first loved us, and the commandment is to love both God and brother
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:19 shows God's prior love as the source of our love, and 4:21 commands that loving God includes loving one's brother, integrating motivation with ethical command.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 John 4:1–3 supports a relativistic view of truth by allowing any confession. What does 1 John 4:1–3 actually teach?
options: It teaches testing spirits to affirm the specific confession that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, rejecting false spirits
It teaches that all spirits and confessions are equally valid
It denies the existence of false prophets
It supports a denial of Jesus’ humanity
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches testing spirits to affirm the specific confession that Jesus Christ came in the flesh, rejecting false spirits
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:1–3 commands believers to test spirits and confirms that only the confession of Jesus coming in the flesh is from God, opposing relativism.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 John 4:5 teach about the source and influence of worldly spirits?
options: They are of the world and speak of the world, and the world listens to them
They are from God but misunderstood
They are neutral and have no influence
They are the same as the Spirit of truth
questions.correctAnswer: They are of the world and speak of the world, and the world listens to them
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:5 teaches that spirits not from God are worldly and communicate worldly messages that the world accepts.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 John 4:17 specifically demonstrate regarding Christian hope and judgment?
options: Perfect love enabling boldness in the day of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Perfect love enabling boldness in the day of judgment
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:17 states that perfected love allows believers to have boldness at the day of judgment, showing God's loving character as the basis for confidence.

questions.question: How does 1 John 4:6 contribute to the understanding of spiritual discernment within the Christian community?
options: By stating those who know God hear the apostles, distinguishing the spirit of truth from error
By suggesting all teachings are equally valid
By denying any distinction between truth and error
By limiting knowledge of God to a select few
questions.correctAnswer: By stating those who know God hear the apostles, distinguishing the spirit of truth from error
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:6 teaches that hearing the apostles is evidence of knowing God and helps distinguish between truth and error spirits, emphasizing community discernment.

questions.question: What doctrine about confession and divine indwelling does 1 John 4:15 teach?
options: Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God
Confession is unnecessary for divine indwelling
Only baptized believers can have God dwell in them
Confession can be false and still result in God’s indwelling
questions.correctAnswer: Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God dwelleth in him, and he in God
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:15 teaches that confession of Jesus as Son of God is the condition for God’s indwelling and mutual indwelling, highlighting the doctrinal importance of confession.
